question: A 35-year-old woman consulted for the appearance of maculo-papular lesions in the upper limbs without other symptoms. The biopsy of one of them demonstrates the presence of noncaseating granulomas. Blood tests are normal except for an elevation of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) levels. On chest radiography, bilateral hilar adenopathies are detected. Which of the following considers the most appropriate attitude?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "35-year-old woman with maculo-papular lesions" -> "biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas" -> "elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) levels" -> "bilateral hilar adenopathies on chest radiography" -> "findings suggest sarcoidosis" -> "corticosteroids are first-line treatment for sarcoidosis" -> "start treatment with corticosteroids orally" -> 85%

analysis: The clinical presentation, including maculo-papular lesions, noncaseating granulomas on biopsy, elevated ACE levels, and bilateral hilar adenopathy, is suggestive of sarcoidosis. In cases of sarcoidosis with significant symptoms or organ involvement, corticosteroids are typically the first-line treatment. Given that the patient has skin lesions and elevated ACE levels, starting treatment with corticosteroids is appropriate. Therefore, the most suitable option is to start treatment with corticosteroids orally.
